CapEx in the US is skyrocketing:

The value of US nondefense capital goods shipments, excluding aircraft, jumped +11.6% YoY in September, reaching a record $86 billion.

This marks the fastest annual growth rate since July 2021.

Even more impressive, shipments have risen at a 3-month annualized rate of +16.5%, the strongest pace since 2011, excluding the pandemic recovery.

Since October 2024, shipments have increased by +$12 billion, or +16.5%.

Much of this momentum is being fueled by the AI investment boom.

Orders for computers, servers, storage devices, and related equipment have surged +27% YoY, the largest annual increase since January 1997.

The AI infrastructure buildout is beyond massive.

US mortgage demand is down to historic lows:

US purchase mortgage applications index fell -2% last week, to 131 points, its 2nd-lowest since January 2025.

This also marks the 6th-lowest weekly reading since 1995, down -32% since January.

As a result, US mortgage applications are now -50% below the pre-pandemic levels seen in 2019.

This comes as the 30Y fixed mortgage rate has risen +120 basis points since February, to 7.18%, near its highest since November 2023.

Rates have now been above 7.0% for 7 consecutive weeks.

The US housing market is frozen.

BREAKING: The Fed’s balance sheet expanded +$3 billion in the week ending November 4th, to $6.75 trillion, its 3rd-highest level since mid-March 2025.

Total assets have surged +$212 billion since the December 2025 low.

Over this period, Treasury holdings have risen +$390 billion, to $4.58 trillion, their highest since March 2024.

At the same time, holdings of Mortgage-Backed Securities have declined -$170 billion, to $1.88 trillion, their lowest since June 2020.

The Fed's balance sheet stands now +$2.99 trillion, or +80%, above pre-pandemic levels.

The Fed's balance sheet is growing again.

Thursday was a historic session in the US options market:

US put option trading volume on CBOE surged to a record 11.23 million contracts on Thursday.

This surpassed the previous all-time high of 10.22 million contracts set on April 4th, 2025.

As a result, the 20-day average of put option volume rose to ~7 million contracts, near its highest on record.

By comparison, the 20-day average oscillated around 4 million contracts in 2022.

8 of the 10 highest daily put option volume readings have occurred in 2026.

We are seeing unprecedented options activity right now.

BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase since Q3 2025.

This also marks its 3rd consecutive quarterly improvement.

Nonfarm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, surged at a +3.7% annualized rate, the strongest growth rate since Q3 2025.

Hourly compensation rose at a +2.9% annualized rate.

As productivity growth outpaced hourly compensation, unit labor costs, which measure labor costs per unit of output, declined -0.7% last quarter, the first quarterly decline since Q2 2025.

This largely a product of companies investing heavily in AI, software, and equipment to improve efficiency, increase output, and contain labor expenses.

AI is catalyzing a major US productivity surge.

Berkshire also revealed that it has been a net buyer of stocks in 2026, with net purchases hitting +$11.2 billion YTD.

This compares to net stock sales of -$10.6 billion over the same period in 2025.

Berkshire is deploying capital again.
